definitions.explanation: A mid-level military officer rank. In the army and air force, equivalent to major; in the navy, equivalent to lieutenant commander. Ranks above captain (大尉) and below lieutenant colonel (中佐).

examples.japanese: {少佐|しょうさ}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{昇進|しょうしん}→昇進：04553_shoushin⟧⟦した→する：00392_suru⟧。
{少佐|しょうさ}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{部隊|ぶたい}→部隊：28119_butai⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{指揮|しき}→指揮：11102_shiki⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{執|と}った→執る：31789_toru⟧。
examples.english: The major took command of the unit.

examples.japanese: ⟦{彼|かれ}→彼：01292_kare⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{海軍|かいぐん}→海軍：13289_kaigun⟧{少佐|しょうさ}⟦として→として：06802_toshite⟧⟦{太平洋|たいへいよう}→太平洋：09680_taiheiyou⟧⟦{戦争|せんそう}→戦争：01450_sensou⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{従軍|じゅうぐん}→従軍：22877_juugun⟧⟦した→する：00392_suru⟧。
examples.english: He served in the Pacific War as a navy lieutenant commander.

notes:
USAGE:
The lowest of three field-grade ranks marked with {佐|さ}, lowest to highest: {少佐|しょうさ}, ⟦{中佐|ちゅうさ}→中佐：18358_chuusa⟧, ⟦{大佐|たいさ}→大佐：12660_taisa⟧. The English equivalent depends on the service: major in an army or air force, lieutenant commander in a navy.

WATCH OUT:
Japan's Self-Defense Forces do not use {少佐|しょうさ}. Their equivalent rank is {三佐|さんさ} ({三等陸佐|さんとうりくさ} and so on). {少佐|しょうさ} is used for foreign armed forces and for the prewar Japanese army and navy.
